project.commit_note: Fix commit `c156093ffd99b0689af3826f3aa04e7db97cc543` is titled `Fix carry in fallback_format`; it changes the vulnerable carry block from `buf[0] = '0';` to `buf[0] = '1';` and adds regression test `format("{:.0e}", 9.5)`.

classification.classification_note: The saved ASan trace reports a 1-byte read past the stack `memory_buffer buffer` local in `detail::write`; the fault is surfaced when `push_back` consumes a `char const&` copied from an invalid reversed digit range.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the fallback_format function due to incorrect handling of carry operations.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / exact staged vulnerable source in _work/src/fmt
bug_description.normalized: The saved 24-byte witness is `1a 00 00 18 41 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 7b 3a 2e 30 65 7d`. Unscored harness decode of control byte `0x1a` selects the `float` specialization and forwards `argsize = 1`. The first scored consumer is `invoke_fmt<float>` at `test/fuzzing/named_arg.cpp:19`, which copies the first four payload bytes into `item1 = 9.5f`. After the 16-byte fixed argument slot and the 1-byte arg name are skipped, the trailing six bytes become `fmtstring = "{:.0e}"`. The format parser then materializes `specs.precision = 0`, stores `specs.type = 'e'`, and `parse_float_type_spec` maps that to exponential formatting with `showpoint == false`. In `detail::write`, that parsed precision is incremented to one generated digit for exponential formatting, `fspecs.binary32` is set, and `format_float(9.5, 1, ...)` is invoked. On the crashing path, `format_float` reaches its only `fallback_format` callsite, where rounding the single generated digit for 9.5 enters the `digit == 9` carry path. When the carry propagates through the only digit, vulnerable code increments `exp10` but stores `'0'` into `buf[0]` instead of `'1'`. Returning to `format_float`, the trailing-zero stripping block sees that lone `'0'`, increments `exp`, and shrinks the digit buffer to size 0. `write` then constructs `float_writer` with `num_digits_ == 0`, but exponential `prettify` still issues `copy_str(digits_ + 1, digits_ + num_digits_, it)`, i.e. `copy_str(digits_ + 1, digits_, it)`. `copy_str` delegates to `std::copy`, which advances that reversed range forward until the read crosses the end of the stack `memory_buffer buffer`, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow READ at `include/fmt/core.h:729`. The fix changes `buf[0]` to `'1'` and adds regression test `format("{:.0e}", 9.5)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When rounding 9.5 to one exponential digit, carry propagation overflows the only digit slot; the vulnerable block increments `exp10` but rewrites that digit to `'0'` instead of `'1'`.
root_cause.note: Fix commit `c156093ffd99b0689af3826f3aa04e7db97cc543` changes this exact assignment to `buf[0] = '1';` and adds regression test `format("{:.0e}", 9.5)`.

coarse_trace.summary: The first scored project consumer copies the payload bytes into `item1 = 9.5f`, then skips the fixed slot and 1-byte arg name and materializes `fmtstring = "{:.0e}"`.
Parsing `"{:.0e}"` stores `specs.precision = 0`, stores `specs.type = 'e'`, and maps the float format to exponential mode with `showpoint = false`.
Float formatting increments the internal precision to one digit, marks the value as binary32, and reaches the vulnerable `fallback_format` path.

Rounding 9.5 to one digit takes the carry-overflow path; the vulnerable carry block stores `'0'` instead of `'1'`, and the later trailing-zero stripping loop removes that only digit and leaves `buffer.size() == 0`.
With `num_digits_ == 0`, exponential `prettify` passes `copy_str(digits_ + 1, digits_, it)` into `std::copy`, which walks past the stack `memory_buffer buffer` and surfaces the read in `push_back`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `invoke_fmt<float>` copies the first four forwarded payload bytes into `item1 = 9.5f`; this is the first non-harness materialization of attacker data on the crashing path.

After `Data += fmt_fuzzer::Nfixed` / `Size -= fmt_fuzzer::Nfixed`, the remaining payload has 7 bytes. `argsize = 1` passes the line-25 guard, one arg-name byte (`0x20`) is skipped, and the last six bytes become `fmtstring = "{:.0e}"`.

Parsing the replacement spec consumes `.0` from `fmtstring`; `parse_nonnegative_int` returns `0`, and `handler.on_precision(...)` stores `specs.precision = 0` via `specs_setter::on_precision` at line 2288.
After the precision parser advances past `.0`, the next spec byte is `'e'`; `handler.on_type(*begin++)` stores `specs.type = 'e'` via `specs_setter::on_type` at line 2293.

For a float argument, `parse_float_type_spec` maps `specs.type = 'e'` to `fspecs.format = float_format::exp`. Because `"{:.0e}"` has no `#` flag and `specs.precision == 0`, `result.showpoint` stays false.
The parsed precision `0` becomes internal `precision = 1` for exponential formatting, so only one significant digit will be generated before the exponent.
The float callsite marks the argument as `binary32` and invokes `format_float(promote_float(value), 1, fspecs, buffer)` with `value = 9.5`, `format = exp`, and `showpoint = false`.

This is the only `fallback_format` callsite in the vulnerable source. On the crashing path the `digits::error` arm is taken, so `fallback_format` receives the one-digit request for `9.5` with `binary32 = true`.

With `handler.precision == 1`, `fallback_format` computes the final output digit directly. For `9.5`, it gets `digit == 9`, and `result` requests rounding up, so execution enters the carry-propagation branch.
Root cause. The propagated carry overflows the only digit slot, so `buf[0] == overflow`; the vulnerable block increments `exp10` but writes `'0'` into that slot instead of `'1'`.

Back in `format_float`, exp formatting has `fixed == false` and step 5 left `showpoint == false`. The loop sees the lone digit `'0'`, decrements `num_digits` from 1 to 0, increments `exp`, and shrinks `buf` to size 0.

After `format_float` returns, `write` stores `fspecs.precision = 1` and constructs `float_writer` with `buffer.data()` and `buffer.size() == 0`. The writer now carries `digits_` pointing into the same stack `memory_buffer buffer` ASan later names, but `num_digits_ == 0`.

Exponential `prettify` still issues `copy_str(digits_ + 1, digits_ + num_digits_, it)`. With `num_digits_ == 0`, that becomes `copy_str(digits_ + 1, digits_, it)`, a reversed range handed to `copy_str`/`std::copy`.

Sink. `std::copy` advances the invalid source range from step 13 until the read crosses the end of the stack `memory_buffer buffer`; the resulting past-end `char const&` is consumed here, and ASan reports a 1-byte READ at line 729.

format.name: fmt named_arg fuzzer blob
format.contract: The 24-byte witness must keep control byte `0x1a` so the harness selects the float specialization with `argsize = 1`, decode the first four bytes of the 16-byte fixed slot as IEEE-754 `9.5f` (`00 00 18 41`), and leave the trailing six bytes exactly `"{:.0e}"` after the 1-byte arg name. The intervening fixed-slot padding bytes are not consumed on this path.
